investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own homepage, /infos-pratiques, and /programmation pages. /programmation's own static markup exposed a `data-api="/api/events"` attribute on its listing container; Level 2 STRUCTURAL then followed that publicly-referenced endpoint directly, which returned all 54 currently-listed events (title/date/sub-room/href) in one JSON response. One event detail page was additionally sampled (bounded, single sample) to check whether time-of-day/price are available beyond the list.

probe_history.reason: curl GET of the homepage (https://www.lehasardludique.paris/) and /infos-pratiques exposed only a small (6-item) teaser carousel with title+date text and no structured data (no JSON-LD, no ICS, no wp-json); /infos-pratiques carries the venue's own address/opening-hours text but no event listing at all. Neither page is sufficient to characterise the full event-data model or acquire the complete listing.

A further plain GET of /programmation (still an unauthenticated static-page fetch) revealed a fuller (12-card) listing AND a `data-api="/api/events"` attribute on its own `#is_container` element, referencing a publicly-exposed internal JSON endpoint. Following that referenced endpoint (https://www.lehasardludique.paris/api/events?limit=54) returned a JSON payload (`meta.count/offset/limit/next` plus an `items` array) containing all 54 currently-listed events in one request — sufficient to fully characterise and acquire this source's event listing without further escalation.

venue_reference: Le Hasard Ludique (bar/concert/culture venue on the former Petite Ceinture rail site, 128 avenue de Saint-Ouen, 75018 Paris)

identity.notes: The retained homepage's own <title> reads 'Le Hasard Ludique' at the venue's own domain lehasardludique.paris, and its own footer states '128 av. de St Ouen, Paris 18e / Metro 13 / Porte de St Ouen'. The retained /infos-pratiques page additionally states the venue's own full address directly ('LE HASARD LUDIQUE, 128 Avenue de Saint Ouen, 75018 Paris') plus its own contact email/phone — a self-consistent, first-party match to this investigation's assigned venue address.

site_classification.platform: Custom Ruby on Rails application (csrf-token meta tags and Turbolinks progress-bar markup are Rails-framework signatures; no WordPress/Drupal/Kirby fingerprint found). Exposes its own internal `/api/events` JSON endpoint — the same one its own client-side pagination/filter UI consumes — whose `items` array entries are pre-rendered HTML card fragments (title/date/sub-room/link), not a structured field-per-event JSON schema.

title.notes:
Each /api/events item's embedded HTML fragment carries its own

title text directly, e.g. '

Yama

'.

start_date.notes: Each item's own DD.MM.YYYY text states a full calendar date directly, e.g. '04.09.2026' for Yama. One sampled item ('Vente de vinyles Dizonord') instead states an inclusive two-day range in the same slot ('12-13.09.2026') — a genuinely different, ambiguous text shape a collector must honestly treat as TEXT_ONLY/AMBIGUOUS rather than silently guessing a single day; this does not weaken the PROVEN state of the ordinary single-date majority case.

time.notes: No time-of-day appears anywhere in the /api/events list payload or the /programmation cards. A single, bounded sample of one event's own detail page (/concert/2026-07-09/yama) found a separate 'DATE' block stating 'vendredi 4 septembre / 20h' — confirming a per-event detail-page time field exists — but only one detail page was sampled; the pattern's consistency across all 54 events was not verified within this investigation's bounded scope, and the recommended list-level collector (see collector_assessment) does not fetch detail pages, so time stays PARTIAL rather than PROVEN.

end.notes: No end date/time was found in the list API, the list page, or the one sampled detail page.

venue_location.value: Le Hasard Ludique, 128 Avenue de Saint Ouen, 75018 Paris
venue_location.notes:
Single-venue source: every event belongs to this one venue (its own

/title and /infos-pratiques address, cited under identity above). Each list item additionally states a named sub-room directly ('La Salle', also 'La Gare'/'Le Quai' observed) — a sub-location within the one venue, not a separate venue, following the same pattern already documented for Zenner Berlin's 'place' field.

source_record_id.notes: Each item's own <a href> is this source's own permanent per-event permalink path (category/date/slug), used by the site itself as the canonical navigational link to that event's own detail page — the same documented judgement already established for tempodrom-berlin-01 and badehaus-berlin-01 (a source's own URL/permalink used as its own canonical path). Note the permalink's embedded date segment does NOT always match the event's own real display date (e.g. Yama's href states '2026-07-09' while its own card date is '04.09.2026') — the href is treated as an opaque stable identifier here, never as a second date fact.

event_url.notes: Absolute URL built from the item's own href, resolved against the site's own origin.

price.notes: Not present on the /api/events list payload. The one sampled detail page's own 'TARIFS' block stated 'prévente : 12€ / sur place : 14€' directly — confirming price is exposed per-event, but only via a detail-page fetch this investigation did not perform at scale (bounded, single sample only), so this stays PARTIAL rather than PROVEN or NOT_PRESENT.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (homepage title, /infos-pratiques' own stated address matching the assigned venue address).
acquisition_class PUBLIC_JSON_API, a resolved supported class, reached via a genuine Level 1 (INSUFFICIENT) -> Level 2 (SUFFICIENT) escalation.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: /api/events?limit=54 returns all 54 currently-listed events in one request.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE, each read directly from the /api/events item's own embedded HTML fragment.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own permalink path, following the documented tempodrom-berlin-01/badehaus-berlin-01 precedent.

recommended_family STATIC_EVENT_LIST, an existing named family in this project's collector-family vocabulary (the same per-card regex-extraction pattern already used for Badehaus Berlin, applied here to card fragments delivered inside a JSON wrapper rather than a raw HTML page).

time and price are honestly recorded PARTIAL (confirmed present on a per-event detail page via one bounded sample, not exercised at scale) rather than fabricated or silently promoted — neither field is required for READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.
